INTRODUCTIONM
In this lesson, you will learn about microwave antennas.
Antennas are the devices used to radiate electromagnetic energy into space and pick up electromagnetic energy from space.
The basic principles of operation are the same for microwave antennas as they are for lower frequency antennas.
However, because of the short wavelength of microwaves, microwave antennas can be more readily designed for high gains and directivity.

DISCUSSION
Microwave antennas radiate electromagnetic energy from the waveguide into space - transmitting.
They also pass electromagnetic energy to the waveguide from space - receiving.

using an analog multimeter, the needle will move off scale to the left. Disconnect the test leads to ensure that the meter movement is not damaged. The voltage level IN THIS measurement is low and should not damage your multimeter.
Microwave antennas have the same characteristics as other antennas. Let's review these characteristics one at a time.
One method to determine the efficiency of an antenna is to measure its ability to couple or radiate energy into space.
This is called POWER GAIN or POWER RATIO.
The power gain of an antenna is the ratio of its radiated power to that of a reference antenna using the same input signal.
For example, if the radiated power of an antenna is twice that of the reference antenna, the antenna has a power gain of 2.

The efficiency of an entire transmitting or receiving system depends largely on impedance matching between the waveguide, antenna and space. If the system is efficient, all the energy is transferred out of the system and into free space.

using an analog multimeter, the needle will move off scale to the left. Disconnect the test leads to ensure that the meter movement is not damaged. The voltage level IN THIS measurement is low and should not damage your multimeter.

If it is not efficient, then some of the energy is reflected back up the waveguide. This energy is called a standing wave. Measuring the standing wave ratio gives the efficiency of the entire transmitting or receiving system...

The Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) is obtained by comparing the voltage levels of the transmitted wave to the levels of the reflected wave at some particular point. The maximum reading divided by the minimum reading is the VSWR. The Current Standing Wave Ratio (ISWR) is handled in the same way.....

An OMNIDIRECTIONAL antenna radiates and receives RF energy in all directions at one time. These antennas have low directivity.

Microwave antennas are normally directional. They have high directivity that concentrates power in one or two directions.
A unidirectional antenna has its directivity in one direction and a bidirectional antenna has its directivity in two directions.
Directional antennas increase power gain because the power is concentrated in a smaller space. Less power is required to cover the same distance.

using an analog multimeter, the needle will move off scale to the left. Disconnect the test leads to ensure that the meter movement is not damaged. The voltage level IN THIS measurement is low and should not damage your multimeter.
Reciprocity is the ability of an antenna to act as a transmitting or receiving antenna.
Antenna reciprocity is possible because the antenna characteristics are essentially the same regardless of whether the antenna is transmitting or receiving energy.
Reciprocity allows most communication and RADAR systems to use one antenna for both receiving and transmitting.

The feed horn is the most commonly used antenna for microwaves......................
Horns are constructed in a variety of shapes and sizes. The shape and dimensions determine the electromagnetic field pattern.
Horn antennas match the impedance of the waveguide to the impedance of space. This reduces standing waves and improves the efficiency of the system.
The gradual expansion of the mouth provides the impedance matching.
Horn antennas also direct the electromagnetic energy in one direction, unidirectional.
This increases the power gain, or efficiency, of the antenna.
Horn antennas have a very high reciprocity, that is, they can be used for transmitting or receiving.
They are used primarily in microwave repeater stations.
The antenna used with the Nida Model 330 Microwave Trainer is a horn that has a power gain of approximately 15 dB.
Another type of microwave antenna is the parabolic reflector.
It consists of a radiator (which can be a horn antenna) and a parabolic reflector called a dish.
As a transmitting antenna, a microwave signal is placed at the focal point (F) by a radiator.
The field departs the radiator and is reflected by the dish.
Due to the shape (parabolic) of the dish, all paths from F to the reflector and to the line XY are of the same length.
The result is a very narrow beam which increases the power gain and directivity over a simple horn antenna.
As a receiving antenna, microwave signals that are directed to the dish are reflected to the focal point (F) or the radiator.
This increases the signal level at the focal point.
Very weak signals that normally could not be picked up by a simple horn antenna are easily received by a parabolic reflector antenna.
Parabolic reflector antennas are used to cover long distances by placing all the available power into a very narrow beam.
For example, communications between earth stations (like home TV dish antennas) and satellites cover long distances. Like a home TV dish antenna.

There are also variations to the full parabolic reflector antennas that are used primarily in RADAR systems.
The only difference in the antennas is the shape of the reflector.
The orange-peel parabola is used where a highly directive pattern in the vertical plane and a somewhat broader pattern in the horizontal plane is desired.
This pattern is desirable for height finding radar systems.
The truncated parabola is a section of a full parabola.....
If the reflector is truncated (cut) so that it is shortened vertically, the radiated beam then spreads out vertically instead of being focused.
However, the beam is narrow in the horizontal plane..lane.
Because of the narrow horizontal pattern, this reflector is used to determine an object's bearing.
The wide vertical beam allows objects at different altitudes to be detected without tilting the antenna.
If the reflector is truncated so that it is shortened horizontally , the radiated beam spreads out horizontally.
However, the beam is narrow in the vertical plane..lane.
This type of reflector is used to determine elevation of objects due to the narrow vertical pattern.
Such a fan-shaped beam is used to determine elevation very accurately. ithout rotating the antenna.
The cylindrical parabola radiates a beam of energy that is wider in one dimension than the other.
This type of antenna is used in search radar and ground control approach radar systems.
The last type of antenna we will cover is the lens antenna.
Lens antennas convert radiated energy into a plane wave in a given direction by using a radiating source with a collimating lens.
The radiating source is normally a horn radiator or a basic dipole antenna.
The collimating lens forces all radial segments of the wavefront into parallel paths by changing the phase velocity of the electromagnetic energy.

The velocity of electromagnetic energy through metals is not the same as in air. This means that, like light, when the electromagnetic energy encounters a boundary where it changes from one medium to another, it refracts...
Because of the concave construction of the lens, wavefronts arriving near the ends are refracted more than those arriving near the middle.
There are many other types of microwave antennas. Most are similar to the horn, parabolic or lens antennas.
